gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-linear-b: Modern in feel, Noto Sans Linear B sends a smooth, unobstructed path around each bend, a plain sans that sits easily beneath Oswald's strong display rows. A long passage flows without snagging.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-manichaean: Modern and clean, this pairing has a clear split. Oswald packs its confident display rows tightly, while Noto Sans Manichaean, a plain sans, keeps its e crossbars open-mouthed for a lighter texture.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-mongolian: Neutral and modern, Noto Sans Mongolian flares its terminals outward beneath Oswald's confident, tightly knit display lines, a sans-serif with a gentle spread. Give it a little extra size.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-lue: Oswald stands tall, confident and tightly knit. Its strongest quality is the gap beside Noto Sans New Tai Lue, a sans-serif whose round letters look cupped rather than clenched.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nko: Tight, strong, then see-through. Oswald packs its display rows into a confident block, and over a long passage Noto Sans NKo, a plain sans, lets light through every c opening.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Oswald sets a confident, tightly knit tone at the top, with strong display letters that hold their ground. Noto Sans NKo Unjoined, a sans with wide openings on small letters, relaxes beneath it.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-old-south-ara: Oswald stands tall and confident, its rows packed tight. Noto Sans Old South Arabian is friendlier, with curved strokes that stop before turning inward, so shrinking the heading would waste its strength while enlarging the body would lose its softness.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Noto Sans Shavian runs loose and contemporary, its curves never knotting at the ends. Oswald sits above it with tightly knit rows and a strong voice, and if the heading shrank it would lose that punch.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans has big lowercase eyes and tubular strokes, like bent copper pipe, with curves that stop short of closing. Press Start 2P adds pinned-apart, retro letters, and that playful gap against the modern plain sans is what gives the pair its charm.
gen-righteous-gf-vend-sans: Bowls that fill the line give Righteous its commanding, fun shape, like thin steel rod bent into every letter. Vend Sans follows with a ruler-drawn, constant-width line and wide, unclosed curve endings; enlarge it too much and the heading loses its lead.
gen-tourney-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi reads neutral and clean, its e opening clearly to the right. Tourney does the bold, athletic shouting with stretched tracking and bulky small letters, while Yaldevi's outsized lowercase handles the quieter work of carrying the text.
gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk is approachable, with a big open-looking e and a, tall bowls and terminals that never close in. Metamorphous brings the commanding side, its thickness shift felt more than seen.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-saira: Love Ya Like A Sister is expressive and bold, its ascenders barely clearing the x-height and its terminals pointing outward. Saira steadies it with rounded letters stretching high and a visible gap in each s.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-n: Oswald packs its rows tightly and speaks with confidence. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation lets its terminals stop far from the stem, so a long passage feels clean, modern and unhurried.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-roboto: Grandstander keeps a pencil-line consistency, short ascenders and a tall x-height, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Roboto follows with generous mouths on its round letters, a clean counterpart.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Eater is dark and aggressive, with thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems and a gentle ebb and flow of weight. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Tai Tham stays quiet.
